narrationScript: An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure, but efficient execution is paramount. Efficiency refers to how much time and memory an algorithm uses as input size grows. To compare algorithms systematically, we use Big O notation. This mathematical tool describes an algorithm's growth rate, abstracting away minor details. It tells us how execution time or space scales with input size 'n'. For example, O(n) means linear growth: double input, double time. O(n^2) is quadratic: double input, quadruple time. O(1) signifies constant time, independent of input size. Big O helps predict performance and choose scalable solutions.
